title: Depth reduction for circuits with CNF and DNF gates
statement: Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ inputs whose depth is at least $1$, and suppose each input coordinate $i$ is fed by a Boolean function $g_i \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$, so that $c$ computes the map $x \mapsto c\bigl(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\bigr)$. Fix a width bound $l \ge 1$, and assume that every $g_i$ is computed both by a DNF formula of width at most $l$, each of whose terms contains at most one literal per variable, and by a CNF formula of width at most $l$. Then there exist a number of inputs $m'$, Boolean functions $g'_1,\dots,g'_{m'}$ each presented as a DNF formula of width at most $l$ with the same restriction that no term contains two literals in the same variable, and a circuit $c'$ of depth at most $\mathrm{depth}(c) - 1$, such that $c\bigl(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\bigr) = c'\bigl(g'_1(x),\dots,g'_{m'}(x)\bigr)$ for every assignment $x$.
hypotheses_covered: each input coordinate fed by a Boolean function g_i on n variables
depth of c is at least 1
each g_i has a width-≤ l DNF representation whose terms have at most one literal per variable (and no repeated literals)
each g_i has a width-≤ l CNF representation
replaced:
For a circuit $c$ of depth at least $1$ (with $0 < l$) over gates that each have a width-$l$
DNF representation with duplicate-free, non-repeating-variable terms and a width-$l$ CNF
representation, there exist a fresh gate family $\mathrm{gates}'$ of such width-$l$ DNFs and
a circuit $c'$ of depth at most $\mathrm{depth}\,c - 1$ computing the same function as $c$.
